full_judgment:
2. Short facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are that the writ petitioner is the owner of a business house. The Anti-corruption Commission instituted a case with the Ramna police station against the writ petitioner, his wife and children on the allegations that in his wealth statement he concealed a sum of Tk.12,37,83,927.65 which, he kept in his name and other members of his family and thereby he has committed offence punishable under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Durnity Daman Commission Ain, 2004. The Bureau of Anit-Corruption upon investigation submitted a police report on 4th June, 2008 recommending for the prosecution of the writ petitioner and others under the said provisions of law. 

 3. In course of the investigation of the case, the investigating officer moved an application for freezing the accounts of the writ petitioner maintained with different Commercial Banks before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate allowed the prayer. The writ petitioner challenged the said order by a writ petition before the High Court Division, which made the rule absolute and quashed the order of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. In the meantime, the case record was sent to the Metropolitan Special Judge for trial where Special Case No.5 of 2008 was registered. The Senior Metropolitan Special Judge took cognizance of offence. The writ petitioner thereupon moved the High Court Division a petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceedings of the case. The High Court Division issued a rule and stayed further proceedings of the case which gave rise to Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.11764 of 2008. 

 "I. Whether the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the entire proceeding has been stayed in 561A proceeding and all the actions arising out of the said case will be determined by the Court in the said case in due course and the High Court Division has committed serious error in making the rule absolute which virtually affecting the Miscellaneous Case No. 11764 of 2008.
